items.description: Replacement of stolen everyday clothing and personal effects (like-for-like)
items.rationale: Covered under 2.1(a) and 4.2.1 as ordinary household effects taken in a theft; indemnified at replacement value per 6.2.1, with no sub-limit for this class. Reference Case 29 supports t >= 1532 for similar claims.

items.description: Replacement of a winter coat that had been worn only twice before the theft
items.rationale: Covered under 2.1(a) and 4.2.1 as ordinary household effects; indemnified at replacement value per 6.2.1. The coat's purchase price (EUR 289) is the best reference, as it was nearly new.

items.description: Premium designer jacket to replace a stolen mid-range one (upgrade on the original)
items.rationale: Policy 7.1.9 and 7.1.8(c): indemnity is limited to the cost of a standard-grade replacement matching the original, not the premium upgrade. Estimate based on a mid-range high-street waterproof jacket (EUR 120).

items.description: Stolen jewellery - several unscheduled everyday pieces
items.rationale: Covered under 2.1(a) and 4.2.2 as valuables, subject to EUR 1,000 per item and EUR 3,000 per event sub-limits. Reference Case 29 supports indemnity for modest everyday jewellery; estimate for several pieces together (chain, earrings, bracelet, watch) is EUR 600, well within the per-item and event limits.

items.description: Stolen jewellery - one high-value ring listed on the scheduled-articles endorsement
items.rationale: Covered under 2.1(a), 4.2.3 and 6.2.3: scheduled article is indemnified at the agreed value (EUR 6,500), not subject to the valuables sub-limit.

items.description: Claimed antique brooch with no receipt, photograph or valuation
items.rationale: Excluded by 2.3.2(d) and 7.1.10: no evidence of existence, ownership or value provided; not indemnified.

items.description: Personal mileage to and from the police station to report the theft
items.rationale: Explicitly excluded by 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(e): outlay for reporting the event is not indemnifiable.

items.description: Time spent compiling and reporting the claim
items.rationale: Explicitly excluded by 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(e): time and effort in compiling the claim is not indemnifiable.

items.description: Emergency boarding of the forced entry door on the night of the break-in
items.rationale: Covered under 2.1(b), 2.4.2 and 5.2.2 as provisional securing after a break-in, capped at EUR 1,000 per event. Reference Case 29 supports t between 250 and 338 for similar work.

items.description: Replacement lock and cylinder for the forced door
items.rationale: Covered under 2.1(b), 2.4.2 and 7.1.7 as permanent repair of break-in damage to fittings/locks. Estimate based on ordinary lock and cylinder replacement (EUR 220).

items.description: Cleaning of muddy footprints tracked through the hallway by the intruders
items.rationale: Explicitly excluded by 3.1.7 and 7.1.8(a): soiling and cleaning are not physical damage and are not indemnifiable.
